Re-verify and correct the "Known gaps — the honest inventory" section of /opt/nxeon/docs/DOCUMENTATION.md (starts around line 3769). A previous attempt finished checking all 60+ citations and then died on an API session limit before writing anything, so the file is untouched at commit fd71056 and you start fresh.

This document's whole value is that it can be trusted, and it is currently stale — critically, stale in the REASSURING direction in at least one place, which is the worst possible failure mode for an honesty inventory.

Verification first, editing second. For EVERY entry in both tables ("Fixed since the last audit — verified, do not re-report these" and "Still not true — ranked by what it would cost a customer or admin"):
1. Open the file and line it cites. Confirm the claim still holds and the line number still points at the right code (this repo is edited constantly; `worker/migrate-real.ts` alone moved ~436 lines today).
2. Correct the line number, move the entry between tables, or delete it, based on what you actually find. Never leave a citation you did not open.

Entries I have specific reason to believe are now WRONG — check these first, but trust what you find over my framing:
- **"Still not true" item 1: "There is no UI to save a card, so renewal auto-charge can never fire."** Card auto-charge was shipped since. Check whether `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` (`startCardSetup`, `finalizeCardSetup`, `removeSavedCard`, `settleOutstanding`) now has real callers in `app/` or `components/`. If so it belongs in the Fixed table with the actual call sites cited.
- **"Still not true" item 2: "The hardened firewall is in the file, not in the kernel."** The hardened ruleset WAS applied. Verify against the LIVE ruleset with `nft list ruleset` — do not infer from the script. Note `scripts/firewall.nft` no longer reads `ADMIN_PORTS = { 22, 8006 }`: port 22 was deliberately moved into the public accept set after removing it from ADMIN_PORTS orphaned SSH entirely and tripped the auto-revert. Read the incident comment in that file and reflect what it says now. Confirm whether `:8006` is in fact unreachable from the internet (it currently tests as closed).
- **"Still not true" item 4: "Post-cutover TLS is never retried" (DEAD).** `sslSweep` is now registered in `worker/index.ts`. Check whether `runPostCutoverTls` (`worker/migrate.ts` ~:260) is still reachable only from a commented-out enqueue, and whether the registered sweep covers the case in practice. "The sweep covers it" and "the retry path is still dead" are different statements — the doc must not blur them.
- **Any claim about test coverage or CI.** `test/migration-gate.test.ts` exists and passes; the suite is 129 tests across billing-terms, dunning-schedule, games, growth, migration-gate, migration-sizing, pricing-display-vs-charge, proration, rate-limit, totp, wallet-split. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs typecheck + tests on push and PR. `tsconfig.json` now sets `allowImportingTsExtensions`, so `npm run check` passes for the first time (bare `tsc` always exited 1 on TS5097). Fix anything implying migration scoring is untestable or that there is no CI.

Then ADD to the "Fixed" table the migration defects found by the first real end-to-end rehearsal (2026-07-26) and fixed in commit fd71056. Read the code and cite it accurately — verify each, do not copy my descriptions blind:
- `clean()` stripped newlines and tabs, then six verification paths `.split("\n")` the result. `cleanLines()` now exists beside `clean()` (read both incident comments). Fixed at `resolvesHere`, the `df` tail, and `unitState`'s `systemctl show` parse (now anchors each KEY=value with `^…$`/`m`). Severe consequence: `resolvesHere` was ALWAYS false, so a correctly-pointed domain read as not pointing at the new server and HTTP-01 certificate issuance was unreachable; `NRestarts` was unparseable so the crash-loop detector could never fire.
- The Docker inspect Go template aborted on `{{len .HostConfig.Devices}}`, making docker emit nothing and the container vanish from the inventory. Now guarded, plus an authoritative `docker ps -aq | wc -l` count (`CCOUNT`) so a shortfall is detected instead of reading as "no containers".
- `parseInventory` filtered out containers with unvalidatable name/image, making `planContainer`'s own blockers unreachable.
- The nginx/apache `server_name` harvest scanned comments and un-symlinked `sites-available/`, injecting phantom domains into the score's denominator and making `COMPLETED` unreachable.
- `/home` was in `DEFAULT_PATHS` (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:110`) AND `UNSAFE_EXACT`, so every customer's default selection was silently discarded. Now expanded per-user with collisions named; refused paths reported.
- `preflightUnitExecs` symlinked a missing interpreter and called it "the same program" without comparing versions (Node 20 → 12). Now compares majors via `majorVersion()` and `UnitExecHost.versionOf`/`versionOnSource`; a mismatch blocks with the right install command.
- `judgeMigrationOutcome` ignored `status: "failed"` steps — a failed database restore could score COMPLETED. Now takes `failedSteps` and `unreadContainers`.
- Contradictory DNS advice replaced by one ordered cutover block; certificate issuance stated as automatic.
- `srcInventoryScript` is now exported so its ~120 lines of generated shell are parsed by `sh -n` and `dash -n` in the test suite.
Also in fd71056: `lib/proration.ts` lost `capMonths` (an upgrade→downgrade round trip kept $362.88); `lib/wallet-split.ts` no longer emits a sub-50c card leg to Stripe; `MigrationWizard` now quotes named Docker volume bytes.

Style: match the document's voice exactly — specific, plain, no marketing tone, every claim carrying a `file:line`. Keep the classification vocabulary (WORKS / SIMULATED / UNVERIFIED SUCCESS / SAVED-BUT-UNREAD / DEAD / PARTIAL). Keep "Still not true" ranked by customer/admin cost. Preserve the warning that concurrent agents edit the tree.

Finally, make sure the two outstanding USER actions appear where an operator will see them, since they are the only unrecovered risks: (a) `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` is NXDOMAIN — verified against a public resolver — so platform transactional email is currently UNSIGNED; it needs Mailcow's key for selector `dkim` published, and the stale `nxeon._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` deleted. (b) `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` / `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` is unset, so `nxeon-backup-offsite.service` sits in a deliberate failed state and every backup exists on one chassis.

Do NOT edit any file other than `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`. Do not build, deploy, restart services, or commit. Other agents are concurrently editing `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/proration.ts`, `lib/actions.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`, `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `lib/disk-expand.ts` and files under `test/` — read them but expect churn, and cite what you see.

Report: a table of every entry checked with its verdict (confirmed / line corrected / moved / deleted), what you added, and anything you could not verify and therefore left flagged.

| **A Go template aborted and containers vanished from the inventory** | `{{len .HostConfig.Devices}}` on its own aborts the **whole** `docker inspect` template on "len of nil pointer" — docker then writes nothing and exits non-zero, so under `2>/dev/null` the container produced zero lines and disappeared. Guarded at `migrate-real.ts:947`. Backed by an authoritative `docker ps -aq | wc -l` count emitted as `CCOUNT` (`:965-966`, parsed at `:1112`), so a shortfall is now a named discrepancy (`containersUnread`, `:3850`) instead of reading as "no containers" |

screen.

The panel no longer lies about it — both fields now carry `note="Not wired — and this value disagrees
with the … that panel actually publishes."` and hedged hints (`components/admin/settings/
GeneralPanel.tsx:111`, `:119`) — but editing either still has no effect. The real values are hardcoded
at `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36` (`mail.nxeon.cloud`) and `:41` (`nxeon.cloud`). The comment at
`GeneralPanel.tsx:96-105` records why this must not be wired naively: the stored values disagree with
what the platform actually publishes, so wiring them without first reconciling them would hand every
customer DNS records that do not work **and** make the deliverability self-check fail correct setups.
Reconcile first, wire second.

**8. Domain-ownership verification and the DNS tools use the wrong resolver.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` imports the top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`, used at `:464` and
`:474` — so verification runs against `/etc/resolv.conf` (OVH's cache), not the zone's authority. A
customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there.
`lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does it correctly and is the model to copy. The same bug is in
`app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` (a `Resolver` with no `setServers`) and
`app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts:23` (`reverse` on the default resolver).

longer orphaned — `checkEmailDeliverability` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`) is now called from
`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:579` — so the missing piece is the PTR row, not the entry point.
`components/admin/MailAnalytics.tsx:135-148`'s "DNS & DMARC" card is still static prose, not a check.

**10. Cloudflare connections cannot refresh.** *PARTIAL.* The working scope in `.env:39`
(`dns.read dns.write zone.read`) omits `offline_access`, so Cloudflare issues no refresh token and every
connection dies at `expiresAt` (`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:332` → `CF_RECONNECT`) with no re-auth prompt.
Separately the **code default** scope (`:59`, `zone:read dns_records:edit offline_access`) is a value
Cloudflare rejects, so any deploy that loses that env var reintroduces the "invalid scope" error a
customer hit three times. The two are not interchangeable: one refreshes and is rejected, the other is
accepted and cannot refresh.

**11. ⚠ USER ACTION — platform transactional email is unsigned.** *Live risk, needs a human.*
`dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` is **NXDOMAIN**, verified against a public resolver (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8,
not the local cache — see gap 8 for why that distinction matters). Every message the platform sends —
password resets, invoices, dunning warnings, suspension notices — is therefore **DKIM-unsigned** and
lands in spam or is dropped outright at the large providers. A stale `nxeon._domainkey.nxeon.cloud`
**is** still published and resolves, which makes this look configured at a glance; it is the wrong
selector and signs nothing.

Fix: take the key for selector `dkim` from **Mailcow's API** — mail is Mailcow's, and the local
resolver must not be trusted for this — publish it at `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud`, then **delete**
the stale `nxeon._domainkey` record. Re-verify against a public resolver, not `dig` with no `@server`.

`OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` and `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` are both unset —
the file contains nothing but comments — so `scripts/backup-offsite.sh:101-125` writes
`{"ok":false,"configured":false,"kind":"none","detail":"no OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE or
OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET set"}` to `/tank/backup/status/offsite.json` and exits non-zero. That leaves
`nxeon-backup-offsite.service` in a **deliberate `failed` state** (confirmed: `failed`, since
2026-07-26 06:35 UTC) so the gap is visible in `systemctl` rather than silent.

`/tank` is one pool in one chassis. A chassis loss loses every customer backup **and** the platform's
own disaster-recovery set. Set exactly one of the two variables — not both, which the script refuses at
`:129` — and the timer starts replicating.

override via `payload.ackInUse` (`worker/volumes.ts:1146-1147`, honoured at `:1177`, `:1189`, `:1211`)
and the refusal notification tells the customer to *"confirm the forced detach in the dashboard"* — but
**nothing sets it**: `ackInUse` appears in `worker/volumes.ts` and nowhere else in the tree. Not
`lib/actions-volumes.ts`, not `components/customer/Volumes.tsx`. The escape hatch exists only in the
engine, and the notification points at a control that does not exist.

**14. Volumes are not portable.** *PARTIAL — the framing is stronger than the code.*
`lib/actions-volumes.ts:129` refuses attaching to any server other than `volume.serverId`, and detach
only clears it when the disk did not stay behind (`worker/volumes.ts:1154`). Once a volume holds data it
is effectively pinned to its first server.

failure case.**

`lib/actions-gameplans.ts:221` — so the number is load-bearing on the money path.
